title: Intermittent shuttle rollout calendar and smoke-pad notes — Nov 2027 (draft)
content:
Summary:
This doc is a compact, day-by-day plan for the `intermittent-shuttle` micro-deploy (small cohorts over regions) plus a lightweight smoke-pad checklist and annotated release notes (first-pass). Purpose: exercise traffic-shifting automation, validate telemetry gates, and rehearse fast fallback to blue variant without user-visible errors.

High-level rollout goals:
- Validate regional routing policy for low-latency paths (US, EU, APAC)
- Keep p95 latency SLO within +10% of baseline
- No more than 0.2% user-facing errors introduced during progressive ramp
- Confirm canary autoscale behaves with new batching hint headers

Owners and contacts:
- Release lead: Aisha Patel (eng-release-engineering) — pager DVT on-call 11/05
- SRE run lead: Diego Morales — Slack: #sre-runway
- Observability owner: Priya Singh — dashboard: /dash/rollouts/intermittent-shuttle
- Pager backup: Ethan Zhao

Rollout calendar (first 72h window):
- Day 0 (2027-11-10, 09:00 PST): Preflight window. No traffic shift. Run smoke-pad locally against staging.
  - Tasks: deploy artifacts to canary pool (tag: shuttle-2027-11-10), run smoke-suite v1, confirm infra health.
- Day 0 (09:30): Canary push to 1% US traffic (region: us-west-2). Observe 30m.
- Day 0 (10:00): If stable, ramp to 5% (30m observation).
- Day 0 afternoon (13:00): Expand to EU cohort 1% (eu-west-1) for 1h.
- Day 1 (2027-11-11): APAC dry-run 0.5% then 2% (asia-sg); keep eyes on p50/p90/p95 and edge errors.
- Day 2 (2027-11-12): If all cohorts green, gradual ramp to 25% global with autoscale stress test.

Abort and fallback criteria (hard gates):
- Any region: sustained error rate > 0.5% for 10m -> immediate rollback to previous variant and page SRE.
- p95 latency increase > 30% over baseline for 15m -> pause ramp and investigate.
- Tokenization or decoding failures (500-class errors) seen in top-10 request hashes -> rollback.
- Canary CPU/GPU saturation > 90% for 5m during minimal traffic (indicates regression in batching).

Telemetry gates (what to watch):
- Functional: 5xx rate, client-observed failures, top-10 error messages (tagged by route).
- Latency: p50/p90/p95, cold-start frequency, tail-latency spikes by quantile.
- Resource: GPU mem pressure, CPU steal, batch size distribution.
- Quality checks: prompt-level correctness sample (on hold, manual sampling by SEs).

Smoke-pad checklist (run before any traffic shift):
- [ ] Verify image/tag deployed to canary nodes (shuttle-2027-11-10).
- [ ] Run smoke script: scripts/smoke/shuttle-smoke.sh with short prompt set (approx 40 prompts).
- [ ] Validate KV cache warm path: confirm <5ms KV hits in logs.
- [ ] Check continuous-batching header honored (x-rw-batch-hint) in proxy logs.
- [ ] Confirm rollout dashboard shows expected ingestion (no dropped spans).
- [ ] Post-smoke: snapshot tracing ids and attach to this doc.

Release notes — first-pass (for customer-facing release_notes/short):
- Feature: Intermittent shuttle routing — improved regional routing heuristics to reduce median latency for 3p customers by ~8% under mixed workload.
- Improvement: Batching hint header respected by runtime to improve token throughput for short queries.
- Ops: Added an automated fast-fallback lane that drains canary traffic to previous variant and warms standby pools.

Known issues (to call out):
- Small proportion of very long-context requests may see an extra 10–20ms decoding overhead in APAC when batch merging coincides with prefix cache refresh. Investigating.
- Observability: our sampling for request body is still conservative — will add richer prompt-level sampling if rollout is successful.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who owns the customer comms if we need to escalate? (suggest: Solutions Eng on-call or PS lead)
- Add Linear ticket for post-rollout quality sweep (REL-XXXX).
- Confirm that Dedicated fleets in customer labs (test accounts) are excluded from canary routing — Diego to validate.

Post-release (72h) checklist:
- [ ] Complete the 24h and 72h telemetry digest and tag any regressions.
- [ ] Run synthetic regression eval (small promptset) and compare against baseline embeddings/outputs.
- [ ] Create a short retro note in this doc with timestamps and links to incident records if any.
- [ ] Promote image to stable channel and tag release branch (after 72h green).

Appendix — quick ops commands and links:
- Smoke script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/blob/main/scripts/smoke/shuttle-smoke.sh
- Canary PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/889
- Linear: https://linear.app/RL/issue/REL-1892 (rollout infra followups)
- Slack watch: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234567 (thread: #release-shuttle)

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep the first APAC step tiny; network jitter in singapore region can mask decode regressions.
- If batch size distribution skews to <2 tokens frequently, suspect header loss between proxy and runtime.
- Consider a temporary traffic-split test with traffic mirroring (non-user visible) if we want to run deeper validation without affecting users.

---
Please edit inline for any missing runbook links, and add ownership for customer comms if you take it. This remains a living draft — will convert to final runbook if green after the first rollout.
